title: One band makes the torus from a loop of rings
subject: Networks of rings joined by shared contacts, read with the canonical knot test on their space-time law
conclusion: Inserting one band into a loop of n equally spaced rule-60 rings, each new ring joined to its partner by two contacts, one on each side, gives the n x 2 torus; every n x m torus with n >= 3 and m >= 2 has a half-turn at every contact exchanging its rings, so the loop, the n x 2 torus and every later torus keep every contact persistent at every lag. A uniform local law, insert a band, makes the torus from a loop at its first step with every stage balanced.
